plan.title: feat(hooks): every write-gate deny prints exactly one next command

narratives.Description: feat(hooks): every write-gate deny prints exactly one next command
narratives.Overview:
1. Inventory tied to the type (P1). In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, one exhaustive record `HOOK_DECISION_CODE_CLASS: Record<HookDecisionCode, "write-deny" | "other">` classes every member of the `HookDecisionCode` union, so a new code does not compile until it is classed. Each `write-deny` code that has more than one cause declares its causes in the same file. A test in `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/` walks the record and fails when a `write-deny` code, or one of its causes, has no row in `table.ts`.
2. Structured cause and one row (P1, P2). The write-path deny constructor takes an optional `cause` value; the dispatcher sets it where it already knows the cause (for example `prospective-scope-cover-deny`: unresolved target, index-changing commit, staged paths unreadable, coverage failure). The printed row id is `<code>` or `<code>:<cause>`. `formatDeclaredRefusal` (`packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/print.ts`) selects that row and quotes substituted values for the shell. The reason code itself is unchanged.
3. Exactly one command (P2). Every write-deny row in `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts` holds exactly one remedy command: the next step. A row whose next step only the operator can take says so in its line; a row whose runnable form does not exist yet uses the existing `deferred` field. A deny prints one row line, for the first red in gate order. A table test asserts one command per write-deny row.
4. Remedy postconditions. `remedy-runs.test.ts` gets a per-row executor and postcondition: by default the refused operation stops refusing; for destructive git the postcondition is that the recovery command succeeds and the original destructive command is still refused in the current checkout.
5. Destructive git (P3). The destructive-git deny prints its row (the linked-worktree recovery command) through the helper, and its own recovery text is removed.
6. Advisory sites (P4). The existing advisory sites (merge-gate warnings for ritual, scope, positive-allow, story-fence and staged-scope; declared warn-mode lines) keep their conditions and verdicts. Where one of them warns for a write-deny code, it prints that code's row line with the host `Warning:` marker and allows. The hook's verdict comes from its own decision, never from the row's `mode`.
7. Existing refusals are declared with `mode: enforce` and an `exception` reason ("existing refusal; only its printed next step changes"); rows already in warn mode stay warn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, an exhaustive `Record<HookDecisionCode, ...>` classes every decision code as write-deny or other, and declares the causes of each multi-cause write-deny code.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/`, a test fails when a write-deny code or one of its causes has no row in `table.ts`.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, each write deny carries its cause and prints exactly one row line, for the first red in gate order, with its reason code unchanged.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/print.ts`, the row is selected by `<code>` or `<code>:<cause>` and substituted values are quoted for the shell.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts`, every write-deny row holds exactly one command, marked as an operator step or `deferred` when the agent cannot run it, and existing refusals are declared `enforce` with an `exception` reason.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/remedy-runs.test.ts`, each row runs with its own postcondition, and the destructive-git row requires the original destructive command to stay refused.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, the destructive-git deny prints its linked-worktree recovery through the table row instead of its own text.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, existing advisory sites keep their conditions and verdicts and print the same row line with the `Warning:` marker when they allow.
narratives.Constraint:
- A hand-kept write-deny list checked only against the table (comment 6991188073, finding 1).
- Treating one printed command as proof the deny is cleared, or packing several commands into one string (comment 6991188073, finding 2).
- Choosing a row variant from message text, or a second remedy map in the dispatcher (comment 6991188073, finding 3).
- Taking the hook verdict from the row's `mode` (comment 6991188073, finding 4).

issueCommentThread.body: Companion floor design: #6138. Point 2 of #5966 is absorbed here.

Scope note from the design arc on #6281 (2026-11-16).

The operator confirmed on #6281 (record comment https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6281#issuecomment-6907733092) that this issue now carries the coverage of refusals that already exist: each one names its gate and prints a remedy that runs as written. #6281 covers only new refusals and the three remedies from #5977.

Constraint for this issue's own design: do not build a second map. The candidate design on #6281 (not yet accepted; latest map https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6281#issuecomment-6907737119) has one refusal table, one print helper and one test that runs each printed remedy from the refused state. The reason-code to next-command mapping here should become rows in that table, printed by that helper and walked by that test.

## In plain English
When a hook write gate denies, the agent gets a reason but not one clear way forward. Each red path (lease, ritual age, cache age, scope, fence, destructive git, foreign repository) words its message differently, so agents guess which ceremony to run, run several, or look for a way around the gate.

The recommended fix uses the refusal table that #6281 already shipped. Each write-gate refusal code gets one row whose remedy is exactly one command. The hook prints the row through the existing print helper, the existing remedy test runs it, and a new check fails when a write-gate code has no row. Advisory strengths print the same line without denying.

Pain source: the four pains are the issue's `## Acceptance` items as written (the issue uses that heading). P3 is narrowed to #5937; see Excluded.

## Pains
- P1 — Every write-gate refusal code has a mapped `next_command`; a test enumerates the codes and fails on an unmapped one.
- P2 — A deny never prints more than one command.
- P3 — The #5937 message (destructive git deny points at the linked-worktree recovery path) is produced by the mapping, not by its own text.
- P4 — Advisory strengths print the same line without denying.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- The #5893 half of acceptance item 3 (pin-mismatch recovery text). That message lives in `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` 488 and `packages/core/src/install-health/`: the pin-missing / pin-mismatch path before `decideHook`, owned by the installer/OVPR maintainer (`docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md` §5). Symptoms only; no design here.
- The `target_class` line of the issue's envelope. Target classes are #6138's design, which is not built; this arc prints `reason_code` and `next_command` and does not invent classes.
- Making `deft doctor` or a deny-rate measurement parse the line; the line is stable text, and readers are a later change.

## Constraints (not pains)
- Do not build a second map (comment 6907780266): mapping rows live in `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts`, print through `print.ts`, and are walked by `remedy-runs.test.ts`.
- No new gate, grant, policy flag or verb. Existing refusals keep their decision; only their printed next step changes.
- When two reds coincide, the first in gate order is printed (issue Design).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- Refusal table (#6281): `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts` 1-45 (row: `id`, `gate`, `mode` default warn, `remedy` as ordered commands, `exception`, `deferred`), rows at 57-97 (none is a hook write-gate code today); `print.ts` 17-96 (`formatDeclaredRefusal`, `formatRemedyCommands`, `parsePrintedRemedy`); `remedy-runs.test.ts`; users today: `preflight-gh/pre-push.ts`, `scope-provenance/extra-path-admission.ts`, `scope-provenance/declaration-hides-axis.ts`, `verify-env/verify-hooks-installed.ts`.
- Hook decisions: `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 4710 `decideHook`; deny codes include `foreign-repository-deny`, `occupancy-occupied`, `occupancy-ritual-mismatch`, `prospective-scope-cover-deny`, `ritual-not-ready`, plus codes produced by helper modules (scope, fence, destructive git). 1845-1935 `OPERATOR_REMEDY_GRANT_CODES` and `authzGrantRemedyCommands` print a mint command for some grant denies (#6275).
- Destructive git (#5937): `packages/core/src/hooks/git-destructive-log.ts` and the destructive-git deny path in the dispatcher.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1). One write-gate code list in `dispatcher.ts` (or beside it), the codes `decideHook` can return as a deny on the Write/Edit and recognised Shell paths. Each code has a row in the refusal table whose `id` is the code. A new test in `refusal-declarations` enumerates that list and fails when a code has no row.
- R2 (P2). Write-gate rows hold exactly one remedy command (the table test asserts length 1 for them). The deny prints one line from `formatDeclaredRefusal`: the code and the one command. Where the command depends on state (for example `session:start --rearm` when occupancy admits this actor, else the operator-default-branch exception), the dispatcher picks the one row variant before printing, never both.
- R3 (P3). The destructive-git deny prints its row (the linked-worktree recovery command) through the helper; its own text is removed.
- R4 (P4). Where a write gate runs at an advisory strength (watch or advise), the hook prints the same row line as an advisory and allows.
- These rows describe refusals that already enforce, so each carries `mode: enforce` with an `exception` reason ("existing refusal; only its printed remedy changes"), per #6281.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is there one enumerable list of write-gate deny codes today, or are they spread across helper modules so the test needs another source?
2. The #6281 table allows several ordered remedy commands per row. Is "exactly one command for write-gate rows" compatible with that table and its remedy test, or does it need a different shape?
3. Which write gates have advisory strengths today, and do they share one print path?
4. Is `mode: enforce` with an `exception` the right way to declare existing refusals in the #6281 table?

## In plain English

Write denials leave agents guessing how to recover. Reusing the existing refusal table and printer is sound, but the recommended mechanism cannot bind as written: a single reason code can represent several different problems, and some recoveries require human choices or multiple steps. A table-entry count alone would not prove that every denial prints a useful command.

Answers to Stop 1:

1. There is a central `HookDecisionCode` union, but it includes allows, session events and other decisions—not an enumerable write-denial registry. Helper results also feed denial codes.
2. One-command arrays fit the table. The existing remedy test needs extension: its executor currently supports only `directive install`, and its success condition expects the refused operation to succeed after recovery.
3. Existing advisory behavior includes merge-gate warnings for selected ritual, scope, positive-allow, story-fence and staged-scope failures, plus declared warn-mode budget messages. These converge partly through a warning collector, but are not a general `watch | advise` mechanism.
4. `mode: enforce` with an existing-refusal exception matches the table’s precedent for already-enforcing cases. It must not replace existing conditional warning behavior or convert current warn-mode declarations to enforcement.

All code evidence below was read at `2ff4efe8636ffddad770fa613de76a326060238d`. No tests were run.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Coverage must be tied to actual denial production

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:348–463` defines the mixed decision-code union; `465–475` independently types verdict and code. The `deny` constructor accepts any `HookDecisionCode` at `1474–1489`. Runtime-policy helpers supply codes at `1756–1768`.

**Failure mode:** A new denial can be added to the union and emitted by a helper while being omitted from the proposed separately maintained write-gate list. The list-to-table test still passes. P1’s “every write-gate refusal” guarantee is therefore not established.

**Disposition:** R1 needs a mechanically connected inventory: write-denial construction must require a registered declaration, or an exhaustive classification must account for every decision code and its applicable surfaces. A manually curated list checked only against another list is insufficient.

### 2. blocks-the-design — “One next step” and “complete recovery” are different contracts

**Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:1871–1902` documents that grant recovery under active UAT requires suspension, a grant with an operator-chosen cohort, and campaign restart. `1855–1861` identifies non-grantable operations. `refusal-declarations/table.ts:30–35` already supports explicitly deferred remedies. `remedy-runs.test.ts:91–103` accepts only `directive install`; `246–268` runs printed commands and expects the refused operation to stop refusing.

Destructive git remains denied when aimed at the current checkout (`dispatcher.ts:3470–3517`); creating a recovery worktree is not proof that replaying the original destructive operation should become allowed.

**Failure mode:** Printing only the grant command can immediately fail under UAT. Printing only suspension does not complete recovery. Treating a linked-worktree command as successful recovery by demanding that the original destructive operation pass would test the wrong outcome. Removing operator-only context also risks presenting a grant command as agent authorization.

**Disposition:** R2/R3 need an explicit distinction between an executable next step and complete clearance. Cases requiring human selection need an honest operator/deferred disposition using the existing mechanism. Remedy tests need per-case executors and meaningful postconditions, including continued denial of unsafe original operations. Packing several commands into one string would not satisfy P2.

### 3. blocks-the-design — State-dependent row selection is underspecified

**Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:5509–5560` uses `prospective-scope-cover-deny` for unresolved targets, index-changing commit syntax and failure to read staged paths; `5586–5589` uses it for coverage failure. These require different responses. `refusal-declarations/print.ts:58–77` selects a declaration by ID and then substitutes values; it has no variant selector.

**Failure mode:** R1 requires the row ID to equal the reason code, while R2 proposes choosing a row variant. Without a defined variant identity and structured cause, one generic row gives incorrect guidance, or the dispatcher acquires a second ad hoc remedy map. Inferring variants from English messages would make recovery brittle.

**Disposition:** The design needs a small explicit representation of the failure cause/context and its relationship to the table row. Selection must preserve the original reason code, keep command templates in the existing table, and test each supported variant. Values derived from paths or payloads also need shell-appropriate quoting; the current placeholder substitution is raw string replacement (`print.ts:29–36`).

### 4. sharpens-framing — Advisory migration must preserve existing conditional decisions

**Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:1500–1536` collects merge-gate warnings and declared warning lines. Ritual warnings occur at `2833–2852`; selected scope and positive-allow warnings at `3145–3192`; story-only fence warnings at `1726–1768`; staged-scope warnings at `5498–5508` and `5586–5589`. Other failures at those same gates remain blocking.

The shared printer derives both wording and `proceed` from row mode (`print.ts:81–89`). Host allow output recognizes `Warning:` or the specific kill-force code (`dispatcher.ts:5873–5879`).

**Failure mode:** An enforced declaration formatted unchanged can say “refused” on an allowed operation. Conversely, using its `proceed` field as the hook verdict can override an existing merge-gate exception. Passing the printer’s warn text directly into an allow decision can also lose it because it lacks the host renderer’s `Warning:` marker.

**Disposition:** R4 can retain the shared table, but should name the existing advisory sites and preserve their predicates and host-visible output. Declaration lifecycle mode and the current hook disposition need distinct treatment. No new strength policy is necessary for this slice.

The snapshot contains imperative constraints, including “do not build a second map,” and linked acceptance language. These were evaluated as proposed requirements, not adopted as execution authority. The envelope’s read-only, no-network, no-posting limits governed this critique.

## In plain English
Problem: when a hook write gate denies, the agent gets a reason but not one clear way forward, so it guesses which ceremony to run, runs several, or looks for a way around the gate.

What the critic found: using the #6281 refusal table and its print helper is sound, and one-command rows fit that table. Three parts of the first draft did not hold. A hand-kept list of write-deny codes checked against the table can miss a new deny, so coverage must be tied to the code type itself. "One next command" is not the same as "this clears the deny": some recoveries need an operator choice, and for destructive git the recovery worktree must not make the original command pass, so the remedy test needs per-row postconditions. And one deny code can mean several different problems (for example `prospective-scope-cover-deny`), so the row must be chosen from a structured cause, not from message text. One point was made sharper: existing advisory warnings must keep their own conditions and host `Warning:` output; the row's mode and the hook's verdict are separate things.

Solution this lean proposes: classify every hook decision code in one exhaustive record, so the compiler forces each new code to be classed and a test fails when a write-deny code or cause has no table row. Each deny carries a small cause value; the row id is the code, or the code and cause. Each row holds exactly one command: the next step, marked as an operator step or `deferred` when the agent cannot run it. The remedy test gets a postcondition per row. Advisory sites keep their conditions and print the same row line as a `Warning:`.

What this adds: table rows and one classification record. No new gate, grant, policy flag or verb; existing deny decisions do not change.

What it does not do:
- It does not change the #5893 pin-mismatch text (installer/OVPR maintainer's area) or add the `target_class` line (#6138).
- It does not make `deft doctor` parse the line.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## Bound remedy
1. Inventory tied to the type (P1). In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, one exhaustive record `HOOK_DECISION_CODE_CLASS: Record<HookDecisionCode, "write-deny" | "other">` classes every member of the `HookDecisionCode` union, so a new code does not compile until it is classed. Each `write-deny` code that has more than one cause declares its causes in the same file. A test in `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/` walks the record and fails when a `write-deny` code, or one of its causes, has no row in `table.ts`.
2. Structured cause and one row (P1, P2). The write-path deny constructor takes an optional `cause` value; the dispatcher sets it where it already knows the cause (for example `prospective-scope-cover-deny`: unresolved target, index-changing commit, staged paths unreadable, coverage failure). The printed row id is `<code>` or `<code>:<cause>`. `formatDeclaredRefusal` (`packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/print.ts`) selects that row and quotes substituted values for the shell. The reason code itself is unchanged.
3. Exactly one command (P2). Every write-deny row in `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts` holds exactly one remedy command: the next step. A row whose next step only the operator can take says so in its line; a row whose runnable form does not exist yet uses the existing `deferred` field. A deny prints one row line, for the first red in gate order. A table test asserts one command per write-deny row.
4. Remedy postconditions. `remedy-runs.test.ts` gets a per-row executor and postcondition: by default the refused operation stops refusing; for destructive git the postcondition is that the recovery command succeeds and the original destructive command is still refused in the current checkout.
5. Destructive git (P3). The destructive-git deny prints its row (the linked-worktree recovery command) through the helper, and its own recovery text is removed.
6. Advisory sites (P4). The existing advisory sites (merge-gate warnings for ritual, scope, positive-allow, story-fence and staged-scope; declared warn-mode lines) keep their conditions and verdicts. Where one of them warns for a write-deny code, it prints that code's row line with the host `Warning:` marker and allows. The hook's verdict comes from its own decision, never from the row's `mode`.
7. Existing refusals are declared with `mode: enforce` and an `exception` reason ("existing refusal; only its printed next step changes"); rows already in warn mode stay warn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, an exhaustive `Record<HookDecisionCode, ...>` classes every decision code as write-deny or other, and declares the causes of each multi-cause write-deny code.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/`, a test fails when a write-deny code or one of its causes has no row in `table.ts`.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, each write deny carries its cause and prints exactly one row line, for the first red in gate order, with its reason code unchanged.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/print.ts`, the row is selected by `<code>` or `<code>:<cause>` and substituted values are quoted for the shell.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts`, every write-deny row holds exactly one command, marked as an operator step or `deferred` when the agent cannot run it, and existing refusals are declared `enforce` with an `exception` reason.
- In `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/remedy-runs.test.ts`, each row runs with its own postcondition, and the destructive-git row requires the original destructive command to stay refused.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, the destructive-git deny prints its linked-worktree recovery through the table row instead of its own text.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, existing advisory sites keep their conditions and verdicts and print the same row line with the `Warning:` marker when they allow.

## Reject
- A hand-kept write-deny list checked only against the table (comment 6991188073, finding 1).
- Treating one printed command as proof the deny is cleared, or packing several commands into one string (comment 6991188073, finding 2).
- Choosing a row variant from message text, or a second remedy map in the dispatcher (comment 6991188073, finding 3).
- Taking the hook verdict from the row's `mode` (comment 6991188073, finding 4).

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

When a write gate denies, the agent gets a reason but not a way forward. The reason differs by red path (lease, ritual age, cache age, scope, fence, pin mismatch, destructive git), so the agent has to guess which ceremony to run, and often runs several or finds a way around the gate. Make every write-gate deny print exactly one next command, chosen from the refusal code.

## Evidence

- #5966 point 2: several independent ways to go red, each with its own message and no single next-command aggregator.
- #5937: destructive-git deny messaging should point at the recovery linked-worktree path.
- #5893: the pin-mismatch hook refusal always recommends a global install even when only the project `node_modules` is out of date.
- Dogfood on #6128 (recorded in #6136): agents under repeated reds treated the kill-switch as the unblock because no deny said what the unblock was.

## Design

- One deny envelope: `reason_code`, `target_class`, `next_command`, one line each. The envelope is the same on the host Write/Edit path and the recognized Shell path.
- `next_command` resolves from `reason_code`, never a list. Examples: missing or stale ritual prints `deft session:ready`; expired lease prints `deft session:start --rearm` when occupancy admits this actor, else the operator-default-branch exception; stale cache prints `deft verify:cache-fresh`; pin mismatch prints the local or global install matching where the mismatch is; destructive git prints the linked-worktree recovery path; `foreign-repository` prints the `cwd` to use.
- When two reds coincide, print the earliest in gate order; the second shows after the first is cleared.
- `watch` and `advise` strengths print the same line as an advisory, so the wording is tested before it blocks anyone.
- The envelope is stable text that `deft doctor` and the deny-rate measurement can parse.

## Related

- #5966, #5937, #5893
- #3742 tracker
- Companion floor design issue (filed alongside this one; linked in the first comment)

## Acceptance

1. Every write-gate refusal code has a mapped `next_command`; a test enumerates the codes and fails on an unmapped one.
2. A deny never prints more than one command.
3. #5937 and #5893 messages are produced by the mapping, not by their own text.
4. Advisory strengths print the same line without denying.
